summary: Sol Survivor is a free browser game that turns kids ages 7 to 12 into junior astronauts in command of a base on the Moon or Mars. Players pack a lander under a real weight limit, then choose one plan each day (explore, build shielding, or rest) while tracking oxygen, water, food, power and radiation. Every decision is driven by real NASA data: solar storms from the DONKI database, Mars weather from the Curiosity rover, Moon Trek and Mars Trek maps, and planets from the NASA Exoplanet Archive. A six-chapter campaign teaches one trade-off at a time, and winning a chapter unlocks the next. A built-in dictionary, read-aloud, quizzes and teacher lesson plans make it work in any classroom, with no download or account.
details:
WHAT IT DOES. Sol Survivor is a free browser game where kids ages 7 to 12 command a crewed base on the Moon or Mars, one day at a time. First they pack a lander under a strict weight limit, choosing between power, life support, shielding, food and water. Then each day they pick one plan for the crew (explore, build shielding, or rest) and live with the result. The game tracks oxygen, water, food, power, crew health and radiation dose. Players can also step outside in a 3D view and do the crew's jobs themselves, such as cleaning dust off solar panels to raise the next day's power.
HOW IT USES NASA DATA. Solar storms come from NASA's DONKI space weather database, and a "Today's real Sun" mode sets the radiation risk from current solar activity. Mars missions use daily weather measured by the Curiosity rover (REMS). Landing sites sit on NASA Moon Trek and Mars Trek maps. Crew supply needs come from NASA's life support baseline values. Players can also visit real planets from the NASA Exoplanet Archive, with every estimated value labeled as an estimate. Each record links to its NASA source.
BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT. Most space material for kids is either fun facts or lessons written for adults. Sol Survivor lets a child make the real trade-offs of a mission and see why they matter. A six-chapter campaign teaches one trade-off per chapter, and winning a chapter unlocks the next, so progress rewards understanding. A whole class can fly the same mission with one mission code and compare choices. Teachers get ten lesson plans aligned to NGSS standards, and the game works offline.
TOOLS AND LANGUAGES. JavaScript, HTML and CSS, built with Vite. The 3D base and walk mode use Three.js. Tests run on Vitest, with axe-core for accessibility checks. The game is hosted on GitHub Pages. We used AI coding assistants to help write and test code, and AI assistance to edit our demo video.
HOW IT IS CREATIVE. The game is the lesson: you cannot win a chapter without learning its trade-off. It opens in a simple view with three gauges and plain words, and an Expert view shows every number for older players. Stars and 30 mission badges reward missions, science and study.
WHAT WE CONSIDERED. Reading level and accessibility for ages 7 to 12: an 84-word dictionary with flashcards, a "What is it?" button on science terms, read-aloud, and quizzes. Honesty about data: real NASA values and game estimates are labeled differently. Classroom limits: no download, no account, and offline play.
